event.route-no-primary-derivable: No main-route adapter is assigned and none could be inferred from the system's default route (additional-route interface {secondary_ifindex}) — in "direct" mode, unmatched traffic stays on the additional route. Assign a main-route adapter in "Interfaces & routes".
event.route-mac-anchor-remembered: Remembered the hardware address of the {role} adapter "{adapter}" so it is still recognized after it changes identifiers.
event.route-local-networks-unreadable-addition: Could not read the system route table ({error}) — reporting no local networks for the additional route.
event.route-local-networks-unreadable-screen: Could not read the system route table ({error}) — the local networks screen will show nothing.
event.route-binding-healed-by-name: The saved {role} adapter ({stale_id}) was no longer found; automatically matched it to "{healed_adapter}" ({healed_id}) by name and saved the correction.
event.route-binding-down-no-heal: The {role} adapter ({stable_id}) is present but not usable right now (status: {oper_status}, has address: {has_ipv4}) and no matching adapter could be found — routing for it is stopped.
event.route-binding-not-found: The saved {role} adapter "{display_name}" ({bound}) was not found among the current network adapters — routing for it is stopped.
event.route-binding-no-next-hop: The {role} adapter "{effective_adapter}" (interface {ifindex}) is up but has no gateway, and no next hop could be determined — it cannot be used for routing.
event.route-no-active-rules: No active rules for this user — no additional routes will be applied.
event.route-counter-overlay-live: Active override route: {destination} via interface {ifindex}, next hop {next_hop}, metric {metric} (on additional route: {on_secondary}).
event.route-counter-overlay-missing: No override routes are active — traffic that should use the main connection may still be using the additional route.
event.route-orphan-enum-failed: Could not read the system route table while recovering routes from a previous run ({error}).
event.route-orphans-adopted: Recovered {count} route(s) left over from a previous run.
event.route-killswitch-luid-error: Leak protection: could not resolve the additional route's interface identifier (index {ifindex}): {error} — staying off.
event.route-killswitch-table-unreadable: Leak protection: could not read the system route table, so local-network exceptions are unknown ({error}) — staying off.
event.route-failclosed-table-unreadable: Leak protection: could not read the system route table ({error}) — falling back to the last known local networks.
event.route-failclosed-cached-subnets: Leak protection: using the last known {subnets} local network(s) so the block keeps the LAN reachable.
event.route-secondary-liveness-dead: The additional route's tunnel (interface {ifindex}, next hop {next_hop}) has been unreachable for {window_secs} second(s) — treating it as down and blocking traffic, even though the adapter still looks up.
event.route-first-contact-install-failed: Could not install the immediate route for a newly seen address ({error}) — it will be added on the next routing update.
event.route-no-routing-user: No user to route for right now ({active_count} active) — removing additional routes.
event.route-paused-teardown: Routing is paused for this user (remove-on-pause) — removing additional routes.
event.route-paused-persist: Routing is paused for this user (keep-on-pause) — keeping the rule-specific routes and removing only the overlay routes.
event.route-policy-recomputed: Routes recomputed after a policy change: {added} added, {removed} removed.
event.route-policy-recompute-failed: Recomputing routes after a policy change failed ({error}).
event.prod-settings-enforcement-mode-written: DNS enforcement mode set to {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}, live resolver available: {resolver_live}).
event.prod-settings-verbose-logging-written: Verbose service logging set to {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}, live reload: {live_reload}).
event.prod-settings-dns-via-secondary-written: “DNS through the tunnel” setting saved as {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}).
event.prod-settings-fast-dns-answers-written: Fast DNS answers setting saved as {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}).
event.prod-settings-fake-ip-udp-relay-written: Fake-IP UDP relay setting saved as {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}).
event.prod-settings-rules-lock-written: Administrative rules lock saved as {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}, requested: {requested}).
event.prod-settings-fake-ip-instant-rst-writte: Fake-IP instant reset setting saved as {written} (previous: {prior}, changed: {changed}).
event.prod-mutation-execute-started: Mutation execute started (kind: {kind}, correlation: {correlation_id}, payload size: {payload_size} bytes).
event.prod-mutation-locked: Mutation refused: rule changes are locked by the administrator (kind: {kind}).
event.prod-mutation-security-alert-active: Mutation refused: a security alert must be acknowledged first (kind: {kind}).
event.prod-mutation-preset-parsed: Preset bytes parsed on the service (route: {route}, known sections: {known_sections}, known rules: {known_rules}, unknown sections: {unknown_sections}, unknown rules: {unknown_rules}).
event.prod-preset-candidate-submitted: Preset candidate submitted (revision: {revision_id}, content hash: {content_hash}). A deduplicated id equal to an existing or active revision means no new rules were detected.
event.prod-preset-assembled: Preset assembled into a canonical rule book (size: {rules_json_len} bytes, content hash: {content_hash}). An empty book serializes to about 50 bytes.
event.prod-alert-resign-adopted-tampered: Tamper-alert acknowledgement re-signed revision rows that did not match their stored signature; their current contents are now trusted (alert: {alert_id}, re-signed: {re_signed}, adopted: {adopted}, revisions: {revisions}).
event.prod-alert-resign-ok: Revision rows re-signed after tamper-alert acknowledgement (alert: {alert_id}, re-signed: {re_signed}).
event.prod-alert-resign-failed: Re-signing revisions after tamper-alert acknowledgement failed (alert: {alert_id}, error: {error}).
event.prod-alert-adopt-skipped: The acknowledgement named rows it did not trust: changed since they were shown ({changed}) or not covered by this alert ({ignored}) (alert: {alert_id}).
event.prod-activation-already-active: Submitted content matches the active revision; nothing to activate (revision: {revision_id}).
event.prod-activation-reactivate-historical: Submitted content matched a historical revision; re-activating it (revision: {revision_id}, previous status: {status}).
event.prod-rules-json-parse-failed: Canonical rules-JSON parse failed; treating as no active rules (origin: {origin}, error: {error}).
event.prod-rules-codec-decode-failed: Rules-JSON codec decode failed; treating as no active rules (origin: {origin}, error: {error}).
event.stored-rules-dropped: Dropped {dropped} stored rule(s) no rule set may hold: an address that is never a destination (this host or broadcast), or an application name that is too long, contains a control character or matches every process; the other rules are in force (origin: {origin}).
event.prod-rules-state-db-mutex-poisoned: State database lock was poisoned; treating as no active rules.
event.prod-rules-get-active-failed: Reading the active revision failed; treating as no active rules (error: {error}).
event.prod-networks-store-decision-failed: Could not store the local-network decision for {cidr} ({error}).
event.prod-networks-prune-superseded-failed: Could not prune superseded local-network answers for adapter {adapter} ({error}).
event.prod-networks-refusing-anchor-store-fail: Could not record that a site refuses main-link addresses ({error}).
event.prod-autorule-main-link-checked: Checked whether the suggested addresses answer on the main link, as requested (answered: {answered}, silent: {silent}, indeterminate: {indeterminate}, skipped recently checked: {skipped_recent}, skipped over limit: {skipped_over_limit}, source: {source}).
event.prod-autorule-secondary-reach-checked: Checked whether the additional route reaches the hosts the main link did not (answered: {answered}, silent: {silent}, indeterminate: {indeterminate}).
event.prod-autorule-probe-spawn-failed: Could not start the main-link probe pass ({error}).
event.prod-traffic-address-store-failed: Adapter address store call failed (operation: {op}, adapter: {adapter_key}, error: {error}).
event.prod-traffic-address-persist-failed: Failed to persist the observed adapter address (adapter: {adapter_key}, error: {error}).
event.prod-audit-per-sid-append-failed: Per-SID apply audit entry could not be appended and was dropped (kind: {kind}, error: {error}).
event.prod-diag-log-page-duplicate-positions: Log page positions are not unique; paging can drop entries (duplicates: {duplicates}).
event.prod-coord-activation-audit-append-faile: Audit append failed for an activation event (error: {error}).
event.dns-listener-short-name-completed: Completed short name {label} using the network domain, resolving as {completed} from server {server}.
event.dns-listener-modeb-resolves-caught-up: Mode B: rule-host resolution is keeping up again — answering from the upstream as usual.
event.dns-listener-direct-host-parked-suggesti: Direct host {host} is a parked suggestion for the additional route — left there instead of being steered onto the main route.
event.dns-listener-modeb-direct-host-shared-ad: Mode B: direct host {host} shares every address with an additional-route rule — answered with a virtual address so it stays on the main route.
event.dns-listener-local-resolver-knows-name: A private resolver on this machine ({server}) knows a name the main upstream reported as non-existent.
event.dns-listener-rule-host-ipv6-uncovered: Rule host {host} was queried over IPv6, which this rule cannot cover — its IPv6 traffic leaves outside the rule.
event.dns-listener-modeb-resolve-slots-saturat: Mode B: all {concurrent} rule-host resolve slots are waiting on an unresponsive upstream — serving rule hosts from the cache so the rest of the machine's DNS keeps working.
event.dns-listener-modeb-unrecognised-recv-err: Mode B: an unrecognized error occurred while receiving a query ({error}, {consecutive_errors} in a row) — continuing to serve.
event.dns-stack-modeb-no-signed-in-user: Mode B: no signed-in user yet — staying in reactive mode until sign-in.
event.dns-stack-modeb-armed: Mode B armed: the local DNS resolver ({listener}) forwards non-rule queries to upstream {upstream}, which answered a probe.
event.dns-stack-servers-uncached: Network changes cannot be watched ({error}); every unanswered name re-reads the machine's DNS servers.
event.dns-servers-cache-config-feed-unwatched: DNS configuration changes cannot be watched ({error}); the DNS server list still refreshes when a connection or route changes.
event.dns-stack-changes-unwatched: Network or DNS settings changes cannot be watched ({error}); the local resolver re-reads the connections' DNS domains on every check.
event.dns-stack-short-name-suffixes-unread: The short-name domains could not be read ({error}); the ones read before stay in use.
event.dns-stack-modeb-no-upstream-answered: Mode B was requested, but no upstream IPv4 DNS server answered a probe — staying in reactive mode.
event.power-resume-rebind-requested: Re-resolving the adapter binding on request ({reason}).
event.power-resume-from-sleep: The machine resumed from sleep — re-resolving the adapter binding and re-applying routes.
event.prodmisc-failclosed-state: Leak protection blocking traffic for the additional route: {fail_closed_active}.
event.prodmisc-adapter-infos-failed: Could not read adapter information ({error}) — returning an empty snapshot.
event.prodmisc-adapter-enum-empty-placeholder: Live adapter enumeration ({data_source}) produced no rows — answering with the placeholder dataset instead.
event.prodmisc-route-bindings-load-failed: Could not load route bindings for this user ({error}) — the leak protection banner is suppressed.
event.autorules-authored-over-budget: Application-authored rules exceeded the budget of {budget}; dropped the {dropped} oldest (e.g. {sample}) — a site that still needs one will be offered again.
event.autorules-inbox-accepted: Accepted {accepted} suggested address(es) (e.g. {anchor}) — added to the user's own rules.
event.autorules-inbox-accept-failed: Could not add the accepted addresses to the rules (code: {code}): {error}.
event.autorules-inbox-dismissed: Declined {dismissed} suggested address(es) (e.g. {anchor}) — they will not be offered again.
event.autorules-inbox-restored: Restored {restored} previously declined address(es); {re_offered} are back on the suggestion list.
event.autorules-inbox-erased: Erased {forgotten} suggestion(s) — they may be offered again from scratch.
event.autorules-intake-evidence-restored: Restored companion evidence from before the last restart: {candidates} candidate(s), {anchors} anchor(s).
event.autorules-intake-not-offered-companion-b: Not offering {host}: every measured sighting came inside another page's burst ({companions} companion(s)).
event.autorules-intake-app-offer-stalled: Offering to move {program} onto the additional route: {stalled} of its connection(s) did not complete on the main link.
event.autorules-intake-domain-offer: A second name under {domain} ({host}) fails on the main link — offering the whole domain instead of each name.
event.autorules-ledger-auto-added: Automatically added {added} address(es) a routed site needs (e.g. {anchor}) to the user's own rules.
event.autorules-ledger-serialize-failed: Could not serialize a pending suggestion ({error}) — it will not survive a restart.
event.autorules-ledger-auto-add-failed: Could not automatically add discovered addresses (e.g. {anchor}, code: {code}): {error}.
event.autorules-pending-cap-dropped: Pending suggestions reached the cap of {kept}; dropped the weakest {dropped}.
event.autorules-store-refused-read-failed: Could not read refused suggestions ({error}) — this session may re-offer a host the user already declined.
event.autorules-store-refused-persist-failed: Could not persist {count} refused suggestion(s) ({error}) — the refusal holds for this session only.
event.autorules-store-declined-read-failed: Could not read declined suggestions for review ({error}).
event.autorules-store-declined-undo-failed: Could not undo a declined suggestion ({error}) — it stays refused for this session.
event.autorules-store-pending-read-failed: Could not read pending suggestions ({error}) — this session starts with an empty offer set.
event.autorules-store-pending-persist-failed: Could not persist {count} pending suggestion(s) ({error}) — they will not survive a restart.
event.autorules-store-pending-clear-failed: Could not clear persisted pending suggestions ({error}).
event.autorules-store-companion-read-failed: Could not read saved companion evidence ({error}) — learning starts over for this session.
event.autorules-store-companion-format-mismatc: Saved companion evidence is not readable by this build ({error}) — starting over.
event.autorules-store-companion-persist-failed: Could not persist companion evidence ({error}) — it will not survive a restart.
event.autorules-store-companion-clear-failed: Could not clear saved companion evidence ({error}).
event.autorules-tick-companion-domain-summary: Companion-domain check found addresses a routed site needs: parked {parked}, authored {authored}, pending {pending}, published {published}.
event.verbose-logging-window-ended: Verbose service logging window ended; back to normal logging.
event.verbose-logging-expiry-unarmed: Verbose logging timer could not start ({error}); the window ends at the next service restart.
event.storage-kill-switch-protocols-reset: A stored leak protection protocol selection blocked nothing; every protocol is blocked instead.

audit.clear-disabled-tooltip: The audit trail cannot be cleared by design. Use the Operational tab to clear runtime logs.

signal.broad-suffix-scope: Broad suffix scope (TLD): *.{label} routes an entire top-level domain
signal.moderate-suffix-scope: Suffix scope: *.{label} routes the domain itself and all its subdomains
signal.mass-change-count: Mass change: {count} rule changes at once
signal.secondary-reroute: Rules added to or moved onto the additional route: {rule-count}
signal.unknown-source: Revision source could not be verified
signal.linked-suspicious-delta: Linked import shows a suspicious delta vs the previous check
signal.rule-set-emptied: All {prev-total} previous rules are being removed
signal.high-removal-ratio: {removed-pct}% of previous rules are being removed
signal.overlapping-rules: *.{apex} already covers {apex} itself and every subdomain — a separate exact-name rule is redundant and can be removed, unless it deliberately routes elsewhere
signal.fail-closed-activation: Switching to “Everything via the additional adapter — no leaks”: if that adapter drops, all traffic is blocked
signal.app-rule-unenforceable: No installed program matches these application rules, so they do nothing: {executables}
signal.additional-adapter-unresolved: The additional route's adapter is not found right now: the rules apply, and its traffic stays blocked until the adapter returns
signal.apply-will-be-refused: The service's consistency check rejects this change, so it will not be applied. The reason is in the service log
signal.invalid-rule-value: A rule contains an invalid value: {rules}

mutations.in-progress-tooltip: Another operation is in progress. Wait for it to finish.

errors.rule-cap-exceeded: Up to 9999 active rules are supported. This change would exceed the limit and was not applied.
errors.auto-rule-cap-exceeded: Rules added by the app are limited to 2000, or to as many as your rule set already holds. This change would add more and was not applied.
errors.unsupported-rule-shape: A rule limits an address to one application. That cannot be carried out yet, so the change was not applied. Remove the application or the address from that rule.
errors.control-character: A rule's value or comment contains a line break or another control character. The change was not applied. Remove the character from that rule.
errors.invalid-rule-value: A rule contains a value that is not valid for its type. The change was not applied. Correct the rules marked as errors in the table.
errors.uac-declined: Administrator approval is required to apply this change. The change was not applied.
errors.busy-conflict: Service is busy with another operation
errors.activation-not-recorded: The change could not be saved, so it was not applied. The previous rules stay in effect. Review the changes and apply again.
errors.service-degraded: Service is degraded — try again later
errors.gui-internal: Internal error in the application — the change was not sent
errors.unknown-preset-operation: The rules-file export/parse operation isn't available.
errors.safe-disable-rpc-pending: Safe disable RPC bridge is not wired yet
errors.rules-locked: Your administrator manages the routing rules on this computer, so they cannot be changed here.
errors.security-alert-unacknowledged: Rules cannot be changed until the security alert in Diagnostics is reviewed and acknowledged.
errors.revision-status-mismatch: These changes were already applied — nothing was sent again.
errors.token-already-consumed: These changes were already applied — nothing was sent again.
errors.audit-chain-changed: The audit trail changed after the breaks were shown. Nothing was restarted.
errors.audit-chain-intact: The audit chain is intact — there is nothing to restart.
errors.restart-key-unavailable: The service has no integrity key to seal a restart with, so the audit chain cannot be restarted on this computer.
errors.audit-write-failed: The service could not write to the audit trail.
errors.audit-unavailable: The audit trail is not available in the service.
errors.malformed-payload: The service could not read the change, so it was not applied.
errors.payload-too-large: The file is over the size limit for a rule set.
errors.file-encoding: The file is not saved as UTF-8 text. Save it in UTF-8 and import it again.
errors.too-many-rules: The file holds more rules than a rule set may have. Split it into two files or remove some rules.
errors.match-value-too-long: A value in the file is longer than the limit.
errors.inline-comment-too-long: A comment in the file is longer than the limit.
errors.canonicalize-rejected: A rule in the file does not fit its section, so the file was not imported.
errors.preset-validation-failed: The file could not be checked, so it was not imported.
errors.alert-not-found: The service no longer has this alert.
errors.illegal-state-transition: This alert has already been handled, so it cannot be changed again.
errors.alerts-storage-failure: The service could not read or save the security alerts.
errors.alerts-store-unavailable: Security alerts are not available in the service.

body.section-nav: You have unsaved changes in {section}. Switch sections anyway?
body.window-close: You have unsaved changes. Close the window anyway?
body.app-quit: You have unsaved changes. Quit NetRuleRouter anyway?
body.generic: You have unsaved changes. Continue anyway?

detail.rules-not-applied: The rules on screen have not been applied to the service yet.
detail.rules-not-saved: The rules on screen have not been saved to your rules file yet. The service is stopped, so the file is the only place they can be kept.

accessible.cancel: Cancel and stay on the current view

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.dismiss-all-tooltip: Removes every notice that can be dismissed. Ones that mirror a live state stay until the state itself changes.

app-unresolved.title: App rules applied, but some apps weren't found
app-unresolved.body: NetRuleRouter couldn't find these programs (they may not be installed in a standard location, or aren't running), so their traffic isn't routed by your rules: {apps}. Launch the app, or check the program name in Rules.

strict-killswitch.title: Block-all leak protection is on
strict-killswitch.body: While the additional adapter (VPN) is down, ALL internet is blocked except your local network — including normal browsing — until it comes back. Switch to the best-effort variant in Settings → Routing behavior if you want your main connection to keep working when the VPN drops.

kill-switch-restored.title: Leak protection restored
kill-switch-restored.body: Leak protection was turned back on from your saved settings (the background service had been reset). If you didn't expect this, you can turn it off in Settings → Routing behavior.

service-operation-failed.title: Service action failed: {operation}
service-operation-failed.body: The service did not carry out this action, so nothing changed. Open Settings to try again, or check the logs for the reason.

update-available.title: A new version is available
update-available.body: NetRuleRouter {version} has been released (you are running {current}). Open the download page to update.

auto-rule-candidates.title: Addresses waiting to be added
auto-rule-candidates.body: The service found {count} addresses the sites you routed need.

reason.route-unavailable: The route this connection needed was unavailable.
reason.not-covered-by-rules: No rule covers this connection, so the default action blocked it.
reason.ipv6-blocked: IPv6 is switched off while leak protection is on, so this connection did not go out.
reason.dns-lockdown: This app went to its own DNS resolver instead of the one NetRuleRouter provides, and encrypted-DNS blocking closed it.
reason.unattributed: NetRuleRouter blocked this connection, but could not identify which filter did it.

backlog.title: Blocked while the app was closed
backlog.body: The service blocked {count} connection(s) while neither this window nor the tray icon was running.

unassigned-tunnel.title: The additional route is not assigned
unassigned-tunnel.body: {adapter} is up, but no connection is assigned to the additional route — so the sites your rules send there will not open.

local-networks.title: A local network was found
local-networks.body: {cidr} on {adapter} stays reachable while routed traffic is blocked. Keep it that way?

adapter-choice.title: Choose which adapter to use
adapter-choice.body: Several adapters answer to the saved name, so your rules are not being applied. Pick the one to use: {list}

no-primary.title: Main connection is not set
no-primary.body: Without a main connection there is nowhere to send traffic your rules do not route, so the rules are not being applied.

no-policy.title: Connections are not chosen yet
no-policy.body: The service has no routing settings for you yet, so nothing is being routed. Choose the main and additional connections.

restored.title: Routing is working again
restored.body: Your rules are being applied again. Pages that were refused while the connection was down keep showing the error until you reload them - press F5 on those tabs.

primary-down.title: The main connection is not up
primary-down.body: Traffic that is not routed to the additional connection has nowhere to go until it comes back. Check the cable, the Wi-Fi, or pick another main connection.

secondary-down.title: The additional connection is not up
secondary-down.body: Everything your rules send there is being held until it comes back — that is the protection doing its job, not a fault. Start the connection, or move those rules to the main one.

adapters-unreadable.title: Cannot read the list of connections
adapters-unreadable.body: The service cannot enumerate network adapters right now, so your rules are not being applied. This usually clears itself; if it does not, restart the service.

unknown.title: Your rules are not being applied
unknown.body: The service reported a state this version does not recognise. Open interfaces and routes to check the setup.

adapter-gone.title: The saved connection is gone
adapter-gone.body: The connection your rules were set to use is no longer on this computer, so the rules are not being applied. Pick another one: {list}
adapter-gone.body-empty: The connection your rules were set to use is no longer on this computer, and there is nothing to replace it with right now.

adapter-failed.title: The saved connection is broken
adapter-failed.body: The connection your rules use is still installed, but its driver will not start, so the rules are not being applied. Reinstall it, or pick another one: {list}
adapter-failed.body-empty: The connection your rules use is still installed, but its driver will not start, and there is nothing to replace it with right now. Reinstalling it usually helps.

rules-file-converged.title: Your rules file was brought up to date
rules-file-converged.body: The linked rules file was written differently from the rules in the app, but both described the same routing. The file has been rewritten to match; nothing about what is applied changed.

service-refused.title: The service will not accept this app
service-refused.body: The background service is running, but it refused a connection from this account. That usually means the service was installed by a different user, or it is already serving as many connections as it allows. Reinstalling the service as an administrator, or signing in as the account that installed it, restores the link.

rule-duplicates.title: A rule is set on both routes
rule-duplicates.body: {count} of your rules are enabled on both routes, starting with {sample}. Which one carries the traffic is decided by evaluation order.

app-rule-learning.title: New application rule is settling in
app-rule-learning.body: {apps}: the service is still learning which addresses this program uses, so its first connection attempts may fail. Restart the program if it is already open.

host-unreachable.title: A site does not answer on either link
host-unreachable.body: {host} did not answer through the main link or through the additional one, so moving it would not help and nothing was offered. The problem is most likely on the site's side.

block-reason.dns-lockdown: Blocks of apps using their own DNS
